glosses: Bound by religious rule; belonging to a monastic or religious order (often as opposed to secular).

examples.text: regular clergy, in distinction from the secular clergy
A quarter of a million strong in 1680, the clergy was only half as large in 1789. The unpopular regular clergy were the worst affected.

glosses: Having a constant pattern; showing evenness of form or appearance.
Both equilateral and equiangular; having all sides of the same length, and all (corresponding) angles of the same size
Whose faces are all congruent regular polygons, equally inclined to each other.
Demonstrating a consistent set of rules; showing order, evenness of operation or occurrence.

examples.text: April may be the cruellest month, but I am planning to render it civilised and to take my antibiotics in a regular manner.

glosses: Of a moon or other satellite: following a relatively close and prograde orbit with little inclination or eccentricity.
Well-behaved, orderly; restrained (of a lifestyle etc.).
Happening at constant (especially short) intervals.

examples.text: He made regular visits to go see his mother.

glosses: Following a set or common pattern; according to the normal rules of a given language.

examples.text: "Walked" is the past tense of the regular verb "to walk".

glosses: Having the expected characteristics or appearances; normal, ordinary, standard.

examples.text: “I don’t see how you can write and act such splendid things, Jo. You’re a regular Shakespeare!” exclaimed Beth, who firmly believed that her sisters were gifted with wonderful genius in all things.

glosses: Permanently organised; being part of a set professional body of troops.
Having bowel movements or menstrual periods at constant intervals in the expected way.

examples.text: Maintaining a high-fibre diet keeps you regular.

glosses: Exemplary; excellent example of; utter, downright.
